t2.state: You route a request a user typed to a video editor's assistant to the ONE tool family that must act on it: cut (remove / trim parts of the footage), audio (sound effects or music), shots (visuals over the footage: titles, lower thirds, charts, images, b-roll, screenshots), captions (subtitles on / off / style), export (render the finished file), or none (no editing tool: a question, thanks, a preference to remember, notes).

t2_01.instructions: Which ONE tool family must act on this request? Request: "Cut out all the ums and uhs from my intro clip."

criteria.cut: remove / trim / tighten parts of the footage (editorial cuts, silence removal; get_transcript is the read step for them)
criteria.audio: add or change sound effects or music (library reuse or generation; insert_asset with lane "audio")
criteria.shots: visuals over or between the footage: TSX shots (titles, lower thirds, charts, templates), generated images / video b-roll, captures (insert_asset with lane "broll" / "overlay")
criteria.captions: word-synced captions on / off / style (transcribe_asset is their prerequisite)
criteria.export: render / export the edit to a file
criteria.none: no tool of the five families: answered in chat, or another group (memory, notes, presets, brand, vocabulary, script, accept_proposal)

t3.state: You check a video editor's assistant's work. Answer yes only if the item really does what the request or script line asks, by plain meaning; a loosely related or merely similar item is NOT a match.

t3_01.instructions:
Does this video template do what the request asks?
Template "App Launch Teaser": A launch teaser for your app. A laptop, phone or browser rises with your screenshot sliding into the screen, the name and tagline land, three feature chips pop in one by one, and the call-to-action pill holds as a poster.
Request: "Make a short teaser for my new app that shows the screenshot on a phone and lists three features."

criteria.true: Yes: the item really does what the request or script line asks, by plain meaning.
criteria.false: No: the item does something else, or is only loosely related / merely similar.

t3_02.instructions:
Does this video template do what the request asks?
Template "Before / After": A split-screen comparison. A divider sweeps across the frame and wipes your after image in over the before, overshoots and settles where you set it, while the labels cross-fade and the headline arrives. Both images share one framing, so the comparison stays honest.
Request: "Show my old landing page and the redesigned one with a wipe between them."

criteria.true: Yes: the item really does what the request or script line asks, by plain meaning.
criteria.false: No: the item does something else, or is only loosely related / merely similar.
